clue.text: Crusader with authority to include half tertiary males

indicators.note: one thing including others holds them inside itself, so the authority word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a permit is a document giving authority to do something

indicators.note: only half of the following word is wanted, so the rest of its letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written; only its first four letters are kept
HE is the male pronoun, and plural males give it twice

explanation.surface: A medieval crusader empowered to enlist half the men of some third-rate group.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving an eight-letter word keeps its first four letters; the plural 'males' asks for the pronoun twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter the Hermit was the French priest who preached and led the People's Crusade of 1096.

clue.text: Left-wing enthusiastic journalists turning up in the grasp of a lord are captive survivors

indicators.note: what is in someone's grasp is held inside their hands, so these pieces sit inside the lord

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord
red is the colour of the political left
synonym

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards, backwards

parts.note: EDS, editors, are the journalists in charge

explanation.surface: Keen left-leaning reporters show up in some aristocrat's clutches and become hostages who lived through it.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in the answer is not clued; 'captive survivors' is a description, not a synonym, of a species saved only by zoos and parks.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese deer died out in the wild and survived only in captive herds, first in the imperial park and then in English parks.

clue.text: Devil, cross, in a rage

indicators.note: the cross sits in the rage, placed inside that word

parts.note: to be in a temper is to be in a rage
a T is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: The Devil, angry, is in a fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a second adjective for the angry devil, but it is the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tempter is a traditional name for Satan, who lures people into sin.

clue.text: Something that can't be seen, like "Ghosts"?

definitions.text: Something that can't be seen, like "Ghosts"?

parts.words: Something that can't be seen, like "Ghosts"?
parts.note: surface reading: something invisible, as spirits of the dead are
setter's reading: Ghosts is a drama by Ibsen, and a drama broadcast on the wireless is heard, not seen

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks show Ghosts is a title: Ibsen's play, which could be performed as a broadcast drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama written for sound broadcasting has no visual staging, so its audience never sees it.

clue.text: Headgear for real saint has chemical element

definitions.note: strictly a halogen is any element of one group, such as chlorine

parts.note: the ring of light a saint wears in paintings
gen is slang for genuine, real information

explanation.surface: A true saint's halo comes with a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real' does double duty: real saints wear a HALO, and real gives GEN, short for genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorine, chlorine, bromine and iodine are each a halogen, a reactive element in group 17 of the periodic table.

clue.text: Secretion derived from moorhen

indicators.note: something derived from a source is made out of it, here by rearranging the bird's letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bodily fluid extracted from a waterbird.
explanation.definitionFit: Hormones are chemicals secreted by glands into the bloodstream, such as insulin or adrenaline.

clue.text: Fabulous bird (male) reaches astronomical limit

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad
the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A legendary cock bird soars as far as the edge of space.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roche limit is the closest distance a moon can orbit a planet before tidal forces tear it apart.

clue.text: …to Violet and Edward's at-home

parts.note: someone at home is in
Vi is the short form of Violet
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the clue before: asked along to Vi and Ted's house party.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues from 6 down. The whole clue describes a guest asked to the party, and its pieces give IN, VI and TED; an at-home is an informal party in someone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Being asked to a party by its hosts is exactly what being invited means.

clue.text: Journey with trustworthy weapon keeping one in pre-Great War pact

indicators.note: a thing keeping something holds it inside, so the weapon is split open

parts.note: synonym
leal is an old Scots word for loyal
a long spear carried by a horseman
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A trip carrying a reliable weapon, taken during the treaty years before 1914.
explanation.walkthrough: The one goes just after the first letter of the weapon. Leal is rare outside Scotland and crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy was the treaty bloc formed in 1882, before the First World War.

clue.text: Change form of dance with contemporary heart

indicators.note: a dance with this at its heart holds it in the middle, so it sits inside

parts.note: the reel is a lively Scottish dance
mod is short for modern

explanation.surface: Updating a traditional dance by giving it a modern core.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel something is to reshape it or alter its structure.

clue.text: Put on new material and get better results

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., as with fresh upholstery fabric
second meaning: regain health, or retrieve losses so the results improve

explanation.surface: Improving a performance by bringing in fresh content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New material' sounds like new songs or jokes, but it is fabric for re-covering a sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyphenated it means fitting a fresh covering; as one word it means regaining health or getting back what was lost.

clue.text: Same again and do it with time off

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong or bad, so these letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Repeat the task, and this time take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With time off' reads as having a holiday, but 'off' is the anagram signal for DO IT plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto marks show that the item above is repeated, so the word means the same thing once more.

clue.text: Go to work constraining almost all the six to march

indicators.note: to constrain is to confine, so the work word holds the rest inside it

parts.note: taken as written
op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: almost all of something is everything except the last bit, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: a sestet is a group of six, such as the last six lines of a sonnet

explanation.surface: A boss heading off to work keeps the half-dozen staff in step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The six' is not a number but a group of six lines in poetry, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose-step is a stiff-legged parade march, so to goose-step is to march in that fashion.

clue.text: Little boy keeping the law, a lethal quality

indicators.note: the little boy is keeping the law, holding it inside his name

parts.note: Vince, a short form of Vincent, is a little boy's name
a rule is a law or regulation

explanation.surface: A small lad who obeys the rules has a deadly streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulence is the deadliness or harmful power of a disease or poison.

clue.text: Patricia who plays Johnson's cat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Patricia ..., the English actress
second meaning: the cat that belonged to Dr Samuel Johnson

explanation.surface: An actress taking the role of a famous pet.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one actress cast as the cat; in fact two people share one surname-like name. Patricia Hodge is a British stage and television actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricia Hodge acts on British screens, and Boswell records Dr Johnson buying oysters for his cat Hodge.

clue.text: The arrogance of many hands?

parts.note: surface reading: the conceit of a big workforce or crew
setter's reading: horses are measured in hands, so a tall mount is many hands high

explanation.walkthrough: A hand is four inches, the unit for a horse's height; being on a tall mount is the idiom for haughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on their high horse is behaving with lofty arrogance and self-righteous superiority.

clue.text: Hat played against neighbours

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bowler hat, as Americans call it
second meaning: a local match between two nearby rival teams

explanation.surface: A hat used as a toy in a game with the people next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A derby is the American name for a bowler, and a local derby is a match between clubs from the same area.

clue.text: Person of scale, with money and some territory

indicators.note: only some of the word is wanted, so the rest of it is cut away

parts.note: someone with money is rich
taken as written; only its first three letters are kept

explanation.surface: A wealthy landowner with a bit of territory is a person of some standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of scale' suggests someone important; it means the man behind a scale of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Richter devised the scale for measuring earthquake magnitude that carries his surname.

clue.text: Attainment of glory in greeting from Mecca, perhaps

indicators.note: the rearranged word sits in the greeting, placed inside it

parts.note: hail is a greeting; Mecca adds the holy setting

indicators.note: perhaps marks the word as only one possible arrangement of its letters, which must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Achieving fame in a salute from the holy city of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose Araucaria clue: 'from Mecca' adds no letters but hints at the holy part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The quest for the cup of the Last Supper made its name an idiom for any supreme goal finally achieved.

clue.text: Hamlet's first speech, not all to his friend

indicators.note: not all of the word is used, so its final letter is dropped
first points to the opening letter of the Danish prince's name

parts.note: the opening letter of Hamlet
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Hamlet's opening words, cut short, addressed to his companion.
explanation.walkthrough: ORATION loses its last letter; 'his' refers back to Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is Hamlet's loyal companion in Shakespeare's tragedy, the one asked to tell his story.

clue.text: Early English doctor went a distance in China for a bit of oyster

parts.note: the li is a traditional Chinese unit of distance
nacre is mother-of-pearl, the lining of an oyster shell

explanation.surface: A Tudor physician travelled far into China in search of oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Linacre was a Tudor physician to Henry VIII who founded the Royal College of Physicians.

clue.text: Matters from minutes ? something wrong in a sailing layout?

definitions.note: the definition completes the phrase matters arising

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the wrong thing is placed in the sailing layout, inside it

parts.note: a rig is the arrangement of a ship's masts and sails
a sin is a wrong act

explanation.surface: Items from a meeting's record: an error in the arrangement of the sails?
explanation.walkthrough: Matters arising is the agenda item for points following from the last meeting's minutes; 'minutes' is not about time.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the fixed committee phrase for business carried over from the previous meeting's record.

clue.text: Italian writings (from the French) on Scottish clan

parts.note: de is French for from
the Camerons are a Highland clan

explanation.surface: Translated Italian texts about a Highland family.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a fourteenth-century Italian collection of a hundred tales.

clue.text: Argentine coming up unchanged

indicators.note: read upwards in this down light the word stays the same, so it reads identically both ways

parts.note: the name of a former Argentine president

explanation.surface: A man from Argentina rises without changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Carlos Menem was president of Argentina from 1989 to 1999.

clue.text: Part of an island or one within call

indicators.note: one thing within another sits inside it

parts.note: hi is a calling greeting
one island: an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: Somewhere on an island, or a single isle within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' means one island, referring back to the definition; a river islet has its own short crossword word.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, sharing it with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Old metal with a measure of purity, no longer with us

parts.note: ex means former
tin is a metal
ct is the abbreviation for carat, which grades gold's purity

explanation.surface: Antique gold of a certain fineness has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct species has died out completely, so it no longer exists.

clue.text: Vehicle turning black and eaten by crow

parts.note: synonym

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A car going dark and getting pecked at by a crow.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrion is the rotting flesh of dead animals, the food of scavengers like crows.

clue.text: More lies fabricated in European capital by Tory group

indicators.note: the made-up words are placed in the capital, inside it

parts.note: Prague is the Czech capital

indicators.note: fabricated things are made up, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Conservatives spreading further untruths in a foreign city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Primrose League was a Victorian Conservative organisation founded in memory of Disraeli, whose favourite flower was supposedly the primrose.
